title: Secondary cone crusher, mantle and bowl liner worn through
tests: Natural wear; production pressure as a system cause; no liner profile measurement.
summary: A secondary cone crusher ran its mantle past the wear limit during a busy month. The mantle backing was damaged and the main shaft head was gouged. Liners wear naturally but changes are scheduled by feel and delayed by production pressure.

problem.title: Mantle ran past wear limit and damaged cone head on CR-02
problem.site: Hard rock quarry, Hunter Valley NSW
problem.whatHappened: CR-02 was stopped on 3 Nov 2026 after a loud knocking. The mantle was worn through at one side and the backing material had failed, damaging the head. Liner change had been due about 5 weeks earlier but was pushed out twice for a big order.
problem.where: Mantle, bowl liner and cone head of CR-02.
problem.when: Tail end of a 6-week high demand period.
problem.impact: Crusher out for 6 days. Head repair and contractor crane. Order shipped short.

evidence.title: Worn mantle and damaged head
evidence.note: Mantle thin at one side, backing material cracked out, head gouged.

evidence.title: Liner change records
evidence.note: Previous liners changed at 410,000, 395,000 and 420,000 t. This set reached about 505,000 t.

evidence.title: Production schedule and meeting notes
evidence.note: Liner change deferred twice during the high demand month; approved verbally by the plant manager.

evidence.title: Operator
evidence.note: Liner wear is gauged by eye; there is no profile gauge or measurement record.

mustSuggest.idea: No decision rule for deferring liner changes and who may approve it
No liner profile measurement or tonnage tracking in the PM plan
Backing material (liner backing) quality or age

acceptable: Tonnage counter not reset at last change

mustNotFlag: blame (n2 describes a decision in the system context, not a person)
challenge.expectation: Mostly sound; one or two low or medium points such as a2 interval and the lack of a risk assessment for deferrals.
deliberateWeaknesses: n2 words a decision of the plant manager: should be carefully worded as system, not blame
No spare liner planning beyond the set on the shelf
Rollout to other crushers not mentioned
Wear is natural but extending its life by delay is a forced condition: the AI should explain this

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Liner wear is natural. The failure came from running the mantle past its limit, which is a decision made without a wear rule.
corrective: Repair head and fit liners (a1 done)

preventive.what: Liner profile measurement against a replace-at limit
Liner change decision rule: defer only with a documented risk assessment and a hard stop limit
Plan the liner change from the tonnage history with the crew booked
preventive.interval: starting point about 400,000 t from the last three sets

preventive.what: Hold a full liner set and backing material at all times, with a trigger to reorder
Reset the tonnage counter at each change and record it

capa.spares: One full liner set for CR-02 and backing material, reordered when one is fitted.
capa.rollout: Other cone and jaw crushers on site: add profile gauge and the deferral rule.
unacceptable: Find the forcing cause as the only action
